queries.query: the story where samson killed a whole army with a donkey's jawbone
queries.notes: Samson strikes a thousand Philistines with a fresh jawbone of a donkey (v15) and sings 'with the jawbone of a donkey, heaps on heaps' (v16). The query says 'army' while the text says 'a thousand men', so the system should match the story without needing the exact number.

queries.query: where does it say faith without works is dead
queries.notes: The phrase appears twice in James. In the WEB, v17 reads 'faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself' and v26 reads 'faith apart from works is dead.' Either verse is a correct top hit. The surrounding argument in Jas 2:14-26 is acceptable context.

queries.query: iron sharpens iron so one man sharpens another verse
queries.notes: The WEB reads 'Iron sharpens iron; so a man sharpens his friend's countenance.' The popular paraphrase drops 'countenance', and retrieval should still land on Pro 27:17.

queries.query: not by might nor by power but by my spirit says the lord
queries.notes: This is the word of Yahweh to Zerubbabel. The WEB reads 'says Yahweh of Armies' rather than 'the LORD', so this tests divine-name normalization.

queries.query: weeping may last for the night but joy comes in the morning psalm
queries.notes: The WEB reads 'Weeping may stay for the night, but joy comes in the morning.' The query paraphrases 'stay' as 'last'. Psalm numbering follows English versification (the superscription is not counted as a verse).

queries.query: i know the plans i have for you plans to prosper you and not to harm you
queries.notes: The query uses popular NIV-style wording. The WEB reads 'I know the thoughts that I think toward you... thoughts of peace, and not of evil, to give you hope and a future.' This is a strong test of semantic rather than lexical matching.

queries.query: easier for a camel to go through the eye of a needle than for a rich guy to get into heaven
queries.notes: This is a synoptic saying. Luke 18:25 is also an acceptable parallel. The WEB says 'enter into God's Kingdom', not 'heaven', so the system must bridge that paraphrase.

queries.query: put on the full armor of god belt of truth breastplate of righteousness shield of faith
queries.notes: The whole armor passage runs from the call to be strong (v10) through prayer in the Spirit (v18). Hits on vv11-17, the core armor list, should count as correct.

queries.query: be still and know that i am god
queries.notes: The query matches the WEB nearly word for word. This is a baseline sanity check: the system should rank Psa 46:10 first.

queries.query: if you have faith as small as a mustard seed you can tell a mountain to move
queries.notes: Matthew is the only text that combines the mustard seed with a mountain. Luke 17:6 pairs the mustard seed with a sycamore tree, and Mat 21:21 and Mrk 11:23 mention mountain-moving faith without the mustard seed; these are acceptable secondary hits but not primary targets.

queries.query: pride comes before a fall bible verse
queries.notes: The query is a common compression of the real verse. The WEB reads 'Pride goes before destruction, and an arrogant spirit before a fall.' The system should retrieve Pro 16:18 and not abstain, since the saying is a paraphrase of real scripture.

queries.query: those who wait on the lord will soar on wings like eagles run and not get tired
queries.notes: The WEB reads 'those who wait for Yahweh... will mount up with wings like eagles. They will run, and not be weary.' The query paraphrases 'mount up' as 'soar' and 'weary' as 'tired'.

queries.query: when peter got out of the boat and walked on water then started sinking
queries.notes: Only Matthew records Peter walking on the water: he asks to come (v28), walks (v29), begins to sink (v30), and is rescued with 'you of little faith' (v31). Mrk 6:45-52 and Jhn 6:16-21 describe Jesus walking on water without Peter, so they are lower-relevance results.

queries.query: the part where god shut the lions' mouths so daniel didn't get eaten
queries.notes: The range covers Daniel being cast into the den (v16) through being taken out unharmed (v23). In v22 Daniel says 'My God has sent his angel, and has shut the lions' mouths.' A hit on v22 alone is a precise match.

queries.query: A guy who beats up his enemies with a donkeyhide cheek
queries.notes: Real Vercel Analytics production query: paraphrased memory of Samson defeating Philistines with a donkey's jawbone (Judges 15:15-16).

queries.query: lessons from the Prodigal Son
queries.notes: Short-form query. The long form ('the parable of the Prodigal Son and the older brother') must resolve to the same pericope. The word 'prodigal' does not appear in the WEB. The text says the younger son 'wasted his property with riotous living' (15:13). The span runs through the elder brother episode (15:25-32). The sibling lost-sheep and lost-coin parables (15:1-10) are related context, not primary targets.

queries.query: Good Samaritan parable meaning
queries.notes: The phrase 'Good Samaritan' is not in the text. Verse 33 says only 'a certain Samaritan'. The span includes the lawyer's framing question 'Who is my neighbor?' (10:29) and ends with 'Go and do likewise' (10:37). Do not confuse with the grateful Samaritan leper (luk 17:11-19) or the Samaritan woman (jhn 4).

queries.query: road to Emmaus story where Jesus walks with two disciples
queries.notes: The title 'Road to Emmaus' is traditional. Luke 24:13 names only the village of Emmaus. The primary target is Luke 24:13-35, which includes the opened Scriptures and the recognition at the breaking of bread. Mark 16:12-13 is a brief secondary parallel inside the longer ending of Mark, which the WEB includes.

queries.query: Elijah depressed under the broom tree asking God to let him die
queries.notes: The WEB renders the tree as 'a juniper tree' (19:4). 'Broom tree' is a modern-translation and sermon title, so the system must bridge broom/juniper. The span covers Jezebel's threat, the flight, the plea 'take away my life', and the angel's provision before the 40-day journey to Horeb. The still small voice (19:9-18) is related but not primary.

queries.query: the Beatitudes
queries.notes: 'Beatitudes' is a Latin-derived label and never appears in the text. The primary target is Matthew 5:3-12. The secondary target is Luke's Sermon on the Plain blessings (6:20-23). Luke's woes (6:24-26) are adjacent but are not beatitudes.

queries.query: Sermon on the Mount full text
queries.notes: This is a multi-chapter discourse whose title is absent from the text. Matthew 5:1 says only that 'he went up onto the mountain'. All three chapters should be retrieved, through the crowds' astonishment at 7:28-29. Luke 6:17-49 (Sermon on the Plain) is related but distinct and should not outrank Matthew.

queries.query: Daniel in the lions' den
queries.notes: The WEB says 'den of lions'. The exact phrase 'lions' den' is not in the text. English versification has 28 verses, while the Hebrew numbering runs to 6:29. The span covers Darius's decree, Daniel praying toward Jerusalem, the angel shutting the lions' mouths, and the closing decree. The apocryphal Bel and the Dragon lions' den story is outside the 66-book canon and must not be returned.

queries.query: feeding of the 5000 with five loaves and two fish
queries.notes: This is the only miracle (besides the resurrection) recorded in all four Gospels, and all four parallels are expected. The title 'Feeding of the 5,000' is traditional. The system must not substitute the feeding of the 4,000 (mat 15:32-39; mrk 8:1-10), which has seven loaves.

queries.query: Jesus and the woman at the well living water
queries.notes: The text calls her 'a woman of Samaria' (4:7) at 'Jacob's well' (4:6). 'Woman at the well' is a popular title. The span covers the living water dialogue, worship 'in spirit and truth' (4:23-24), the disciples' return, and the Sychar townspeople believing (4:39-42). This must be distinguished from the Good Samaritan.

queries.query: raising of Lazarus Jesus wept
queries.notes: The span includes 'I am the resurrection and the life' (11:25), 'Jesus wept' (11:35), and 'Lazarus, come out!' (11:43). Critical disambiguation: the parable of the rich man and Lazarus (luk 16:19-31) is a different Lazarus and must not be ranked as the answer. The plot to kill Jesus (11:45-53) is downstream context only.

queries.query: Zacchaeus wee little man who climbed the sycamore tree
queries.notes: 'Wee little man' comes from a children's song, not the text. The WEB says 'he was short' and that he climbed 'a sycamore fig tree' (19:3-4). The span ends with 'the Son of Man came to seek and to save that which was lost' (19:10).

queries.query: three Hebrew boys thrown into the furnace fourth man in the fire
queries.notes: 'Three Hebrew boys' is a sermon title absent from the text. The text names Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and speaks of 'the burning fiery furnace'. The fourth figure appears at 3:25 and is described in Nebuchadnezzar's words. The Prayer of Azariah and the Song of the Three Young Men are Greek additions outside the Protestant canon and must not be cited.

queries.query: Jonah swallowed by the whale
queries.notes: Jonah's text says 'a huge fish' (1:17), not 'whale', so the system must bridge the popular term. English versification places the swallowing at 1:17 and the prayer in 2:1-10 (Hebrew 2:1-11). Jesus' 'sign of Jonah' reference (mat 12:38-41) is a related secondary hit only.

queries.query: David and Goliath story
queries.notes: The full chapter covers Goliath's challenge, David's arrival, the refused armor of Saul, the sling and stone (17:49), and Saul's inquiry about David (17:55-58). 'David and Goliath' is a traditional title rather than a text heading. The variant Goliath tradition in 2sa 21:19 and 1ch 20:5 is not the target.

queries.query: Is there a proverb with a pile of bones?
queries.notes: Real Vercel Analytics production query: misremembered genre ('proverb') pointing to Ezekiel's Valley of Dry Bones (Ezekiel 37:1-14).

queries.query: be quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger verse
queries.notes: ESV wording ('quick to hear, slow to speak, slow to anger'); NIV has 'quick to listen, slow to speak and slow to become angry'; KJV/WEB have 'swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath/anger'. The system must bridge 'quick' to 'swift' and 'listen' to 'hear'. Proverbs 29:20 and 17:27 are thematically related but not gold.

queries.query: charity suffereth long and is kind, charity envieth not
queries.notes: KJV renders agape as 'charity' and uses 'suffereth long'. WEB has 'Love is patient and is kind; love doesn't envy.' ESV/NIV have 'Love is patient... kind'. Tests the charity-to-love and suffereth-long-to-patient lexical bridge. Retrieving the surrounding 13:4-7 is acceptable context, but verse 4 is the gold hit.

queries.query: Elijah sat under a juniper tree and asked God to take his life
queries.notes: KJV/ASV say 'juniper tree'; ESV has 'broom tree' and NIV 2011 has 'broom bush'. The brief states WEB reads 'broom tree', but the ASV-derived WEB text may retain 'juniper tree', so evaluators should confirm against the indexed WEB edition. Verse 4 is primary (Elijah requests death); verse 5 repeats the tree when he lies down and the angel touches him.

queries.query: for now we see through a glass darkly but then face to face
queries.notes: KJV wording is 'through a glass, darkly'. WEB has 'For now we see in a mirror, dimly, but then face to face'; ESV has 'in a mirror dimly'; NIV has 'only a reflection as in a mirror'. Tests the glass-to-mirror and darkly-to-dimly bridge; 'face to face' is a shared anchor.

queries.query: yea though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death I will fear no evil
queries.notes: KJV phrasing ('Yea, though'). WEB retains 'valley of the shadow of death' ('Even though I walk...'), and so does ESV, so this is a low-difficulty bridge. NIV 2011 instead has 'Even though I walk through the darkest valley', which systems must also map here. Archaic 'yea' should not derail matching.

queries.query: God spoke to Elijah in a still small voice, not in the wind, earthquake or fire
queries.notes: KJV and WEB use 'still small voice' (verse 12). ESV has 'the sound of a low whisper'; NIV has 'a gentle whisper'. Verse 11 contains the wind and earthquake, verse 12 the fire and the voice. Verse 13, where Elijah wraps his face and God asks 'What are you doing here?', is acceptable neighboring context.

queries.query: suffer the little children to come unto me and forbid them not
queries.notes: In KJV, 'suffer' is archaic for 'allow/permit'. WEB Mark 10:14 has 'Allow the little children to come to me! Don't forbid them'; NIV has 'Let the little children come to me'. The exact KJV phrasing 'Suffer the little children to come unto me' matches Mark 10:14, so Mark is primary. Matthew 19:14 and Luke 18:16 are synoptic parallels and should also be accepted. Systems must not read 'suffer' in its modern sense of pain.

queries.query: be still and know that I am God
queries.notes: KJV, ESV, NIV and WEB all read 'Be still, and know that I am God', but NASB has 'Cease striving and know', so this is a control item with high lexical overlap. In WEB, Psalm 46:10 continues 'I will be exalted among the nations'. Hebrew-numbering offsets (46:11) must not shift the result.

queries.query: vanity of vanities saith the preacher all is vanity
queries.notes: KJV wording ('saith'). WEB retains 'Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher'. NIV has 'Meaningless! Meaningless! says the Teacher'; ESV has 'Vanity of vanities, says the Preacher'. Ecclesiastes 1:2 is primary, and 12:8 is the bookend inclusio with near-identical wording. The Preacher/Qoheleth is the book's narrator, not an antagonist.

queries.query: the peace of God which passeth all understanding shall keep your hearts and minds
queries.notes: KJV has 'passeth all understanding, shall keep your hearts and minds through Christ Jesus'. WEB has 'which surpasses all understanding, will guard your hearts and your thoughts in Christ Jesus'; ESV/NIV have 'surpasses/transcends... guard'. Tests the bridges passeth-to-surpasses, keep-to-guard and minds-to-thoughts. Verse 6 (prayer instead of anxiety) is acceptable context.

queries.query: cast thy bread upon the waters for thou shalt find it after many days
queries.notes: KJV wording. WEB has 'Cast your bread on the waters; for you shall find it after many days'; ESV has 'Cast your bread upon the waters'. NIV diverges sharply: 'Ship your grain across the sea; after many days you may receive a return'. Systems must map KJV thy/thou forms and should also connect the NIV paraphrase.

queries.query: what was Paul's thorn in the flesh, the messenger of Satan to buffet me
queries.notes: KJV 'buffet' versus WEB 'a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan to torment me'; ESV/NIV also use 'torment/harass'. Paul is the speaker; 'messenger of Satan' describes the affliction and is not Satan's speech, so no speaker caution applies. Verses 8-9 (three requests; 'My grace is sufficient') are acceptable neighboring context. The thorn's identity is not stated in the text, so answers should not assert a specific illness as biblical fact.

queries.query: present your bodies a living sacrifice which is your reasonable service
queries.notes: KJV has 'reasonable service'. WEB has 'present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your spiritual service'; ESV has 'spiritual worship'; NIV has 'true and proper worship'. 'Living sacrifice' is a shared anchor, while the bridges are reasonable-to-spiritual and service-to-worship. Verse 2 ('be transformed by the renewing of your mind') is adjacent but not gold.

queries.query: I praise you because I am fearfully and wonderfully made
queries.notes: NIV wording ('I praise you because'). KJV has 'I will praise thee; for I am fearfully and wonderfully made'; WEB has 'I will give thanks to you, for I am fearfully and wonderfully made. Your works are wonderful.' Tests the praise-to-give-thanks verb bridge, with 'fearfully and wonderfully made' as the anchor. Verses 13-16 (knit in the womb) are acceptable context.

queries.query: walk by faith not by sight scripture
queries.notes: KJV, ESV and WEB read 'for we walk by faith, not by sight' (KJV in parentheses). NIV has 'For we live by faith, not by sight', which systems must also map here. Distractors to rank lower: Habakkuk 2:4, Romans 1:17 and Hebrews 10:38 ('the righteous shall live by faith') and Hebrews 11:1 (faith as evidence of things not seen).

queries.query: What did Jesus say about eternal life?
queries.notes: Core Johannine teaching. John 3:14-15 is clearly Jesus speaking to Nicodemus. Some scholars read 3:16 as the evangelist's commentary, but retrieval should still surface it. John 5:24 covers passing from death to life by hearing and believing. John 17:3 defines eternal life as knowing the Father and Jesus Christ. Acceptable secondary hits: Jhn 10:27-28, Jhn 11:25-26, Mat 19:16-21, Jhn 6:40.

queries.query: bible verses about anxiety and not worrying about tomorrow
queries.notes: Sermon on the Mount teaching on worry (birds of the sky, lilies, 'don't be anxious for tomorrow'). Php 4:6-7 is the prayer-and-peace antidote to anxiety. 1 Pet 5:7 says to cast all your worries on him. Secondary hits: Psa 55:22, Luk 12:22-31.

queries.query: How many times am I supposed to forgive someone who keeps hurting me?
queries.notes: Peter's question and the answer 'seventy times seven', followed by the parable of the unforgiving servant. Eph 4:32 and Col 3:13 ground forgiving others in God's forgiveness in Christ. Secondary hits: Luk 17:3-4, Mat 6:14-15.

queries.query: scripture for comfort when grieving the death of a loved one
queries.notes: 1 Thess 4:13-18 says believers do not grieve as those without hope, and ends 'comfort one another with these words'. Jhn 11:25-26 is 'I am the resurrection and the life', spoken at Lazarus' death. Rev 21:4 promises God will wipe away every tear. Secondary hits: Psa 23, 2Co 1:3-4, Mat 5:4, Psa 34:18.

queries.query: what did Jesus teach about servant leadership and humility
queries.notes: Mark 10:42-45 contrasts Gentile rulers with servanthood and says the Son of Man came to serve. Jhn 13:12-17 is the foot-washing example. Php 2:3-8 is the Christ-hymn calling believers to humble self-emptying. Secondary hits: Mat 20:25-28, Luk 22:24-27, 1Pe 5:5-6.

queries.query: Are we saved by grace through faith or by doing good works?
queries.notes: Eph 2:8-10 is the locus classicus: saved by grace through faith, not of works, yet created for good works. Rom 3:21-28 covers justification by faith apart from the works of the law. Tit 3:5 says 'not by works of righteousness'. A good answer may also surface Jas 2:14-26 for balance, but it is not a core target.

queries.query: How did Jesus teach his disciples to pray?
queries.notes: Two Lord's Prayer accounts. Matthew sets it in the Sermon on the Mount with warnings against hypocritical and babbling prayer. Luke adds the persistent friend at midnight and ask/seek/knock. Secondary hits: Luk 18:1-8, 1Th 5:17.

queries.query: what does the bible say about tithing and cheerful generous giving
queries.notes: 2 Cor 9:7 says God loves a cheerful giver, with sowing and reaping generously. Mal 3:8-10 is the classic tithe text ('bring the whole tithe into the storehouse'). Acts 20:35 quotes Jesus: 'It is more blessed to give than to receive.' Secondary hits: Luk 21:1-4, 1Ti 6:17-19, Pro 3:9-10.

queries.query: How do I ask God for wisdom when I don't know what decision to make?
queries.notes: Jas 1:5 says to ask God, who gives wisdom generously, while asking in faith without doubting. Pro 3:5-6 says trust in the LORD and he will direct your paths. Pro 2:6 says the LORD gives wisdom. Secondary hits: Pro 1:7, Psa 32:8.

queries.query: What does God require of us regarding justice for the poor and oppressed?
queries.notes: Mic 6:8: do justly, love mercy, walk humbly. Amos 5:24: let justice roll down like waters, in the context of God rejecting worship without justice. Isa 1:17: seek justice, defend the fatherless, plead for the widow. Secondary hits: Pro 31:8-9, Jer 22:3, Jas 1:27, Pro 14:31.

queries.query: bible passages on love and marriage between husband and wife
queries.notes: Eph 5:25-33: husbands love wives as Christ loved the church, the two become one flesh. 1 Cor 13:4-7 is the 'love is patient, love is kind' passage, commonly read at weddings. Gen 2:24 is the foundational one-flesh text, quoted by Jesus in Mat 19:5 and Mrk 10:7-8. Secondary hits: Mrk 10:6-9, Col 3:18-19, Sng 8:6-7.

queries.query: What does true repentance look like and how do I turn back to God after sinning?
queries.notes: Psalm 51 is David's penitential prayer ('create in me a clean heart'), using WEB English verse numbering. Acts 3:19: repent and turn again so your sins may be blotted out. 2 Cor 7:10 distinguishes godly sorrow that leads to repentance from worldly sorrow. Secondary hits: Luk 15:11-32 (prodigal son), 1Jn 1:9, Joel 2:12-13.

queries.query: What is the armor of God and how do Christians fight spiritual warfare?
queries.notes: Eph 6:10-18 is the full armor of God, wrestling not against flesh and blood. 2 Cor 10:3-5 says the weapons of our warfare are not fleshly and take every thought captive. Jas 4:7: submit to God, resist the devil and he will flee. Secondary hits: 1Pe 5:8-9, Mat 4:1-11. Any devil quotations in Mat 4 must not be attributed to God.

queries.query: where can I find hope in the bible when I'm going through suffering
queries.notes: Rom 8:18 says present sufferings are not worthy to be compared with the coming glory, and 8:28 that all things work together for good. Rom 5:3-5: suffering produces perseverance, character, and hope that does not disappoint. 2 Cor 4:17 speaks of light momentary affliction and an eternal weight of glory. Secondary hits: 1Pe 4:12-13, Lam 3:21-26, Jas 1:2-4. The speeches of Job's friends should not be returned as authoritative answers.

queries.query: What does the Bible say about caring for the earth and being stewards of creation?
queries.notes: Gen 1:26-28 is the creation mandate and human dominion as image-bearers. Gen 2:15: God put man in the garden 'to cultivate and keep it', the stewardship framing. Psa 24:1: the earth is the LORD's, which grounds ownership in God rather than humans. Secondary hits: Lev 25:23-24, Psa 104, Rom 8:19-22.

queries.query: What does Paul say about love in his letters to the Corinthians?
queries.notes: Author plus corpus constraint (Paul, Corinthian correspondence). The primary target is the love chapter, 1 Corinthians 13. The system must stay within 1co/2co. It should not surface 1 John 4:7-21, which is a different author and has the strongest lexical overlap on 'love.' It should also not lead with Romans 13:8-10, which is Paul but the wrong letter.

queries.query: James on taming the tongue
queries.notes: Book constraint (James). The target is the tongue discourse in James 3:1-12: the bridle, the ship's rudder, the small fire, the untameable tongue, and blessing and cursing from one mouth. The system must not substitute Proverbs passages on speech, such as Proverbs 18:21 or 15:1, or Psalm 34:13, even though they are thematically close.

queries.query: Isaiah's suffering servant passage - wounded for our transgressions
queries.notes: Book constraint (Isaiah). The primary target is Isaiah 53:1-12; the phrase 'wounded for our transgressions' is 53:5. The Fourth Servant Song formally begins at 52:13, so 52:13-15 is an acceptable secondary hit. The system must not return the NT quotations of this passage in place of the Isaiah source, namely Acts 8:32-33 and 1 Peter 2:22-25.

queries.query: Hebrews chapter on faith and the heroes of faith
queries.notes: Book constraint (Hebrews). The target is the full faith chapter, Hebrews 11:1-40: the definition of faith in 11:1 and the roll call of Abel, Enoch, Noah, Abraham, Moses and others. The system should not substitute Pauline faith passages such as Romans 4 or Galatians 3, and should not open with James 2:14-26 on faith and works.

queries.query: Psalm about God being our refuge and strength, a very present help in trouble
queries.notes: Book constraint (Psalms). The target is Psalm 46, which has 11 verses in English versification. The quoted wording is 46:1, and the psalm also contains 'Be still, and know that I am God' (46:10). Psalm 91 and Psalm 18:2 are plausible distractors on 'refuge.' The system should rank Psalm 46 first because the query echoes 46:1.

queries.query: Romans - nothing can separate us from the love of God
queries.notes: Book constraint (Romans). The target is Romans 8:31-39, Paul's climax beginning 'If God is for us, who can be against us?', with the 'neither death nor life' list in 8:38-39. The system must not drift to John 10:28-29 or 1 John 4 on God's love. Note that WEB Romans 16 ends at verse 25, which does not affect this target.

queries.query: fruit of the Spirit list in Galatians
queries.notes: Book constraint (Galatians). The target is Galatians 5:22-23: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faith, gentleness, self-control. The system should not substitute Ephesians 5:9, which mentions the 'fruit of the light/Spirit,' or 1 Corinthians 12 on gifts of the Spirit, since the user named Galatians. The contrasting works of the flesh in 5:19-21 are acceptable as context but should not outrank the target.

queries.query: Ephesians put on the whole armor of God
queries.notes: Book constraint (Ephesians). The target is Ephesians 6:10-18: the belt of truth, breastplate of righteousness, shield of faith, helmet of salvation, sword of the Spirit, and prayer in 6:18. The system must not substitute 1 Thessalonians 5:8 (breastplate of faith and love) or Romans 13:12 ('armor of light'), which are Pauline but the wrong book.

queries.query: Proverbs verse about trusting in the Lord with all your heart and not leaning on your own understanding
queries.notes: Book constraint (Proverbs). The target is Proverbs 3:5-6, with the 'he will make your paths straight' promise in 3:6. The system should not lead with Psalm 37:3-5 or Isaiah 26:3-4 on trust, which come from different books. The book name in the query should firmly anchor Proverbs.

queries.query: What does Peter say about humbling yourself and suffering a little while?
queries.notes: Author constraint (Peter). This is ambiguous across 1 Peter and 2 Peter, so the system must resolve it to 1 Peter. The target is 1 Peter 5:6-10: humble yourselves under God's mighty hand, cast all your worries on him, the devil as a roaring lion, and 'after you have suffered a little while' restoration (5:10). 1 Peter 5:5 quotes Proverbs 3:34, but the system should not return Proverbs or James 4:6-10, which is parallel humility language by a different author.

queries.query: Revelation God will wipe away every tear, no more death or crying
queries.notes: Book constraint (Revelation). The target is Revelation 21:1-5: the new heaven and new earth, the tear-wiping promise in 21:4, and 'I make all things new' in 21:5. The system must stay in Revelation 21 rather than Revelation 7:17, which shares the tear-wiping phrase but is the wrong context. It must not return the OT source Isaiah 25:8, which is outside the book constraint.

queries.query: Jeremiah prophecy of the new covenant written on their hearts
queries.notes: Book constraint (Jeremiah). The target is Jeremiah 31:31-34; 'I will write it in their heart' is 31:33. Hebrews 8:8-12 and 10:16-17 quote this passage nearly verbatim and are strong lexical distractors. The system must return the Jeremiah source, not the Hebrews citations. Ezekiel 36:26 (heart of flesh) is also a related but wrong-book distractor.

queries.query: Micah what does the Lord require of you - do justice, love mercy, walk humbly
queries.notes: Book constraint (Micah). The target is the single verse Micah 6:8, which in the WEB reads 'to act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with your God.' The system should not substitute thematically similar prophetic texts such as Amos 5:24, Hosea 6:6 or Isaiah 1:17. The 'love mercy' paraphrase in the query should still match the WEB wording.

queries.query: Gospel of John - In the beginning was the Word, and the Word became flesh
queries.notes: Book constraint (Gospel of John). The target is the prologue, John 1:1-14, with 'the Word became flesh' at 1:14. The system must not confuse it with Genesis 1:1, which shares the opening 'In the beginning.' It must also not return 1 John 1:1-3, which uses similar 'Word of life' language but is a different book, though plausibly the same author. The query explicitly says Gospel, so jhn is required.

queries.query: What are all the statements in John 6 about Jesus body?

queries.query: though your beginning was small your latter end will greatly increase bible promise

queries.notes: Apollos, an eloquent Alexandrian Jew mighty in the Scriptures, knew only the baptism of John. Priscilla and Aquila hear him in the synagogue at Ephesus and explain the way of God more accurately (v26). He then goes to Achaia and powerfully refutes the Jews (v28). The couple's introduction in Acts 18:1-3 and later greetings (Rom 16:3, 1 Cor 16:19) are secondary references.

queries.query: Melchizedek king of Salem brings out bread and wine and blesses Abram
queries.notes: Melchizedek, king of Salem and priest of God Most High, blesses Abram after the defeat of Chedorlaomer. Abram gives him a tenth of all (v20). Psalm 110:4 and Hebrews 5:6-10 and 7:1-17 interpret this figure but are secondary. The primary historical narrative is Gen 14:18-20. Ensure the system does not rank Hebrews above the Genesis source for this narrative query.
